stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group on the waiting list

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They hypothesized that phone use would affect attention to the road.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 licensed drivers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

**Results.** The group that talked on the phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 11.4. The group that drove without a phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 4.9. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 90 students were randomly assigned to study 40 vocabulary words either in six ten-minute sessions on different days or in one sixty-minute session. One month later, the spaced group recalled a mean of 27 words and the single-session group a mean of 16 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In an experiment, 120 students read a passage and were randomly assigned either to take three practice quizzes or to reread the passage three times. On a test one week later, the quiz group scored a mean of 68 percent and the rereading group 49 percent (p = 0.01).

**Source C.** In a survey of 600 students, 71 percent said that rereading notes was their main study method, and most rated it as highly effective. Only 12 percent said that they regularly tested themselves.

questions.stem: A drug reduces pain and anxiety by acting at the brain's endorphin receptors. Which type of drug is this?

options.why: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
Correct. An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.explanation: An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.stem: With her eyes closed, Uma can still touch her nose with her fingertip. Which sense makes this possible?

options.why: Correct. Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes proximity?

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object
options.why: That describes closure.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike
options.why: That describes similarity.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background
options.why: That describes figure and ground.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other
options.why: Correct. This is what proximity means.

questions.explanation: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group that drove without a phone
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that talked on the phone
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Correct. Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.explanation: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain?

options.why: Correct. Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.

questions.explanation: Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.stem: A child realizes that water poured from a short glass into a tall one could be poured back to give the same level as before. Which concept does this show?

options.why: Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.
Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.
Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Correct. Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.

questions.explanation: Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The two groups differed in preference for sweetened water at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the type of injection given after drinking
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The rats given the nausea-causing injection were several months older
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: In psychodynamic theory, denial, projection and rationalization are all examples of which of the following?

options.why: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
Correct. A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.explanation: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.stem: A hungry rat presses a lever to get food. The food is which kind of reinforcer?

options.why: A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.
The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
Correct. A primary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as food or water, that satisfies a biological need and is rewarding without learning.

questions.explanation: A primary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as food or water, that satisfies a biological need and is rewarding without learning.

questions.stem: Years of loud concerts destroyed the hair cells in Dee's cochlea. Which kind of hearing loss does she have?

options.why: Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Correct. Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.

questions.explanation: Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes deindividuation?

options.text: The loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity
options.why: Correct. This is what deindividuation means.

options.text: The tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone
options.why: That describes social loafing.

options.text: The reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present
options.why: That describes diffusion of responsibility.

options.text: The improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others
options.why: That describes social facilitation.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: A shy teenager avoids parties, so she gets little social practice, which makes her even more shy. This interaction between thoughts, behavior and environment is called which of the following?

options.why: A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.
Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.
Correct. Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.explanation: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a drug that blocks the reuptake of serotonin to treat a patient's depression. Which kind of drug is this?

options.why: Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
Correct. An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.stem: Instead of studying disorders, Dr. Lim studies happiness, character strengths and what makes life worth living. Which field is this?

options.why: Correct. Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.
Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.
Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.

questions.explanation: Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm?

options.why: Correct. Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.stem: A psychologist says a client's depression comes from a lack of acceptance by others, which has blocked her growth toward her potential. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.
Correct. The humanistic perspective is the view that disorders result from blocked personal growth and a lack of acceptance.
The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.

questions.explanation: The humanistic perspective is the view that disorders result from blocked personal growth and a lack of acceptance.

questions.stem: A witness picks the thief out of a line-up of six people. Which measure of memory is this?

options.why: Correct. Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.
Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.

questions.explanation: Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.

questions.stem: To learn forty new vocabulary words, Felix must concentrate and rehearse them. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.
Correct. Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.
Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.
Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes endorphins?

options.text: The neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure
options.why: Correct. This is what endorphins means.
That describes GABA.

options.text: The brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory
options.why: That describes glutamate.

options.text: The neurotransmitter that enables muscle movement, learning and memory
options.why: That describes acetylcholine.

questions.explanation: Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman?

options.why: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Correct. Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.

questions.explanation: Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 9, 3, 19, 5, 11, 8, 8. What is the mean of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
Correct. Add the scores (63) and divide by 7.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 3, 5, 8, 8, 9, 11, 19. Add the scores (63) and divide by 7. The one very high score pulls the mean (9) above the median (8), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Ed feels strong resentment toward his sister but treats her with exaggerated kindness and praise. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Correct. Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: A manager refuses to interview applicants who are over fifty, whatever their skills. This action is an example of which of the following?

options.why: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Correct. Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.stem: Which receptor cells let a person see the colors and fine details of a painting in daylight?

options.why: Correct. Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.
The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.

questions.explanation: Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the expectation that people will help those who have helped them?

options.why: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Correct. The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.

questions.explanation: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.stem: In multiple sclerosis, the immune system destroys a fatty covering on axons, so messages travel slowly and movement becomes difficult. Which structure is damaged?

options.why: The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
Correct. The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.
A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.explanation: The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage?

options.why: Correct. A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.
An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
A split brain is the condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut.
Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.

questions.explanation: A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.

questions.stem: An elderly man increasingly forgets recent events, gets lost in familiar places and can no longer manage his money. Which term describes his condition?

options.why: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Correct. Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.

questions.explanation: Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: A multiple-choice math question asks students to find the one correct answer. Which kind of thinking does this task require?

options.why: Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.
Correct. Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
Functional fixedness is the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose.

questions.explanation: Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the sudden realization of the solution to a problem?

options.why: A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
Correct. Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.explanation: Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.stem: A coffee shop gives a free drink after every ten purchases. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
Correct. A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.explanation: A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.stem: A charity first asks people to sign a petition and a week later asks the same people for a donation. Which technique is this?

options.why: Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
Correct. The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.
A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.

questions.explanation: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler explores happily while his mother is present, cries when she leaves and calms quickly when she returns. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.
Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.
Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.
Correct. Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.

questions.explanation: Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.

questions.stem: Which sense sends its signals to the brain without first passing through the thalamus?

options.why: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Correct. Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.explanation: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes infantile amnesia?

options.text: The inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life
options.why: Correct. This is what infantile amnesia means.

options.text: A progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities
options.why: That describes Alzheimer's disease.

options.text: The inability to form new memories after an injury or illness
options.why: That describes anterograde amnesia.

options.text: The loss of memories from before an injury or illness
options.why: That describes retrograde amnesia.

questions.explanation: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.stem: As a friend walks away, her image on Tom's retina shrinks, but he does not think she is getting smaller. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.explanation: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.stem: A specialist uses reinforcement step by step to teach a child with autism to communicate. Which approach is this?

options.why: Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Correct. Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.explanation: Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.stem: As well as obtaining permission from the parents, the researchers asked each child whether he or she was willing to take part. What is the child's agreement called?

options.why: Correct. Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.
Deception is misleading participants about the study.
Confidentiality is keeping data private.
Debriefing happens after the study.

questions.explanation: Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes somnambulism?

options.text: A sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep
options.why: That describes narcolepsy.

options.text: Sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what somnambulism means.

options.text: A sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings
options.why: That describes sleep apnea.

options.text: A sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams
options.why: That describes REM sleep behavior disorder.

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes tolerance?

options.text: The need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use
options.why: Correct. This is what tolerance means.

options.text: A drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption
options.why: That describes a reuptake inhibitor.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: That describes withdrawal.

options.text: A drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors
options.why: That describes an antagonist.

questions.explanation: Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.

questions.stem: A child uses one mental category, 'chair', for stools, armchairs and benches. This mental category is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
Correct. A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.
Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.

questions.explanation: A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.stem: The sudden appearance of a snake on the path triggers fear in a hiker. The snake is acting as which of the following?

options.why: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
Correct. An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.explanation: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.stem: A one-year-old says 'milk' to mean 'I want some milk'. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Correct. The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.

questions.explanation: The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes synesthesia?

options.text: The weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: That describes the absolute threshold.

options.text: The smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: That describes the just-noticeable difference.

options.text: The condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense
options.why: Correct. This is what synesthesia means.

options.text: The way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste
options.why: That describes sensory interaction.

questions.explanation: Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.

questions.stem: According to Freud, a person may be unable to recall a painful childhood event because the mind has blocked it from consciousness. What did Freud call this?

options.why: Correct. Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in the facial expression produced by holding a pen
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in amusement at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The group holding the pen between the teeth saw the cartoons in color, and the other group saw them in black and white
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes health psychology?

options.text: The response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support
options.why: That describes the tend-and-befriend response.

options.text: The response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape
options.why: That describes the fight-or-flight response.

options.text: An event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging
options.why: That describes a stressor.

options.text: The field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness
options.why: Correct. This is what health psychology means.

questions.explanation: Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.70, +0.05, −0.93, +0.52. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.05 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.93 is farthest from zero.
+0.52 is closer to zero.
+0.70 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.93 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes long-term potentiation?

options.text: The part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information
options.why: That describes the visuospatial sketchpad.

options.text: The part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words
options.why: That describes the phonological loop.

options.text: The part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts
options.why: That describes the central executive.

options.text: The strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory
options.why: Correct. This is what long-term potentiation means.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of hours worked in a paid job
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

options.text: Conscientiousness score on a personality inventory
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds?

options.why: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Correct. Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.explanation: Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.stem: Gia's relationships swing between adoring and hating the same person; she fears abandonment and acts impulsively. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Correct. Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.

questions.explanation: Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.

questions.stem: A previously healthy student suddenly develops hallucinations after a period of intense stress and later recovers well. Which pattern of onset is this?

options.why: Correct. An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.explanation: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.

questions.stem: Yara loves trying unfamiliar foods, visiting art galleries and exploring new ideas. She would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Correct. Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.explanation: Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The level of stress at home
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The average number of hours slept per night
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: The word 'unkindly' has three meaningful parts: un, kind and ly. Each of these parts is which of the following?

options.why: A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.
Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.
Correct. A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Debriefing happens after the study.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: A therapist stops using a technique when she sees that it is making her client worse. Which ethical principle is she following?

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.
Correct. Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a single-blind procedure?

options.text: A procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition
options.why: That describes a double-blind procedure.

options.text: The measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is
options.why: That describes effect size.

options.text: A procedure in which the participants do not know which condition they are in
options.why: Correct. This is what a single-blind procedure means.

options.text: An improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself
options.why: That describes the placebo effect.

questions.explanation: A single-blind procedure is a procedure in which the participants do not know which condition they are in.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes dream interpretation?

options.text: The psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts
options.why: Correct. This is what dream interpretation means.

options.text: The humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow
options.why: That describes person-centered therapy.

options.text: A state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories
options.why: That describes hypnosis.

options.text: The technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says
options.why: That describes active listening.

questions.explanation: Dream interpretation is the psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts.

questions.stem: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The amount of sleep caused the difference in reaction time
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The amount of sleep and reaction time are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior?

options.why: Correct. Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.
Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.

questions.explanation: Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing?

options.why: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.
Correct. Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.explanation: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes conformity?

options.text: The adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard
options.why: Correct. This is what conformity means.

options.text: A situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone
options.why: That describes a social trap.

options.text: The following of the direct commands of an authority figure
options.why: That describes obedience.

options.text: The tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors
options.why: That describes the false consensus effect.

questions.explanation: Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves?

options.why: Correct. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.

questions.explanation: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: When two brothers fight over a game, their father removes the game, and the fighting decreases. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of attention to the road

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of attention to the road.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Attention to the road was defined as the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. On average, the value was 11.4 for the group that talked on the phone and 4.9 for the group that drove without a phone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 licensed drivers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. (11.4 compared with 4.9).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that phone use affects attention to the road. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to phone use. The finding illustrates selective attention and inattentional blindness: attention is limited, so people fail to notice visible objects when attention is elsewhere.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Spacing study sessions and testing oneself lead to better long-term learning than cramming or rereading.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who spread their study over six days recalled 27 of 40 words a month later, compared with 16 for students who studied in one session.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the spacing effect: distributed practice gives repeated chances to encode and consolidate the material, so it is retained longer than with massed practice.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who took practice quizzes scored 68 percent a week later, compared with 49 percent for students who reread the passage.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the testing effect: retrieving information from memory strengthens the memory and its retrieval cues more than rereading does.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
